model_conventions.checked_scope: The direct admitted arrival/work and stationary Palm constructions are checked through the active queueing route. The convention covers only the source-stated admitted-stream normal form. It does not assert a raw-path or empirical-frequency theorem, and it does not credit an unproved raw-to-admitted transport.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source itself states the independent admitted Poisson streams at rates s after thinning, together with iid unit-mean exponential work. The active Lean route constructs that admitted-stream/Palm model directly at the stated rates and uses it for GPS/FCFS replay.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source writes the admitted-stream law explicitly, but the current library does not yet prove a pathwise raw-marked survivor re-enumeration, multiclass pushforward equality, selected-Palm transport, and response-functional correspondence. Calling the direct carrier a derivation from the raw carrier would therefore be false; taking the explicitly stated post-thinning law as the model normal form is precise and does not weaken a named paper conclusion.

model_conventions.checked_scope: PaperInterface.lean makes both the global steady-operation condition and the target-local margin visible. SLA2026GPSParameters.lean derives the stronger all-cell/aggregate facts only inside the fixed-load-feasible policy bridge. The stationary selected-Palm GPS/FCFS proof uses the visible global condition plus the target margin and does not treat the fixed-load bridge as an unconditional source derivation.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For the selected Borough's SLA subsystem, Lean makes explicit the full-system well-definedness regularity implicit in the source's GPS/steady-operation language: nonnegative capacity, positive SLA weights, total weight at most one, and total SLA admitted load below capacity. The displayed target tail margin remains the separate condition s_target < C phi_target. Always-backlogged no-guarantee background work is excluded from the SLA load sum because it receives only residual capacity.
model_conventions.source_locator: cited publication:541-543; cited publication:600-602; cited publication:628-639
model_conventions.why_needed: The standalone display explicitly states only the target-local margin, while the active remote-past construction needs a stable full SLA subsystem. The source's positive admitted streams and GPS active-set allocation make zero weight for any SLA class incompatible with a well-defined stationary full queue, and aggregate slack is needed for stationarity. The later fixed-load program proves stronger all-cell margins only for policies satisfying its own quantified SLA constraints, together with the positive SLA parameter recorded at :600-602; it cannot silently strengthen the standalone display. This convention exposes the implicit global regularity and keeps its dependency direction honest.

reviewed_proof_scopes.semantic_scope: The source's explicitly stated post-thinning independent admitted-Poisson/iid-work normal form, steady ideal-fluid GPS/FCFS model, selected admitted-request tail inequality, logarithmic sufficient SLA inequality, and fixed-load optimization program. This review checks the displayed tail-to-SLA algebra, sign orientation, model-carrier scope, and the separation between the display's target-local margin and the later fixed-load submodel. It does not call the unproved raw-carrier-to-admitted-Palm transport a derivation.

The reciprocal-capacity reformulation: convexity after restricting to the positive feasible region, necessity by summing the cellwise service margins, sufficiency by explicit Borough capacity and weight construction, and the equality-chain argument for binding-case uniqueness.

The all-request cost, total efficiency, within-category range objective, and the two endpoint arguments: the Cauchy--Schwarz equality characterization for the efficient SLA and the positive-affine cost construction, existence, and binding argument for the efficiency-best zero-range SLA.

The price-of-equity proof: normalized capacity shares at binding endpoints, the Pearson chi-square identity, the constructive equitable upper bound, the zero-price equivalence, and the capacity-rescaling argument under categorywise fixed noninspection burden.

The centralized reciprocal program, its square-root optimum, the strict per-cell SLA comparison under positive loads and at least two Boroughs, and the algebra reducing centralization-gain-versus-price comparison to the normalized effective-load and chi-square inequality.
